title: Notion Custom Agents: What the Credit Pricing Means for Your Team
body_md:
![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-custom-agents-2026s-most-overhyped-ai-tool/1.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/pricing))*

Notion's Custom Agents are pitched as AI teammates that run on schedules or triggers so your team doesn't have to do the repetitive work. The technology works as described, but it runs on a metered credit system, so agents that fire constantly in the background cost more than occasional ones. Whether that overhead is worth it depends on how often an agent runs and how much work each run replaces. Notion's own published examples put per-run costs at roughly $0.03 to $0.30 depending on the agent type, so do the math before scaling.

Here are the mechanics, based on Notion's pricing and help pages (linked at the end).

## What's Actually Going On

![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-custom-agents-2026s-most-overhyped-ai-tool/2.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/buy-and-track-notion-credits-for-custom-agents))*

### Custom Agents are a metered product bolted onto a per-seat plan

Custom Agents are available to Business and Enterprise customers, priced under the Notion credit system, which they moved to on May 4, 2026. This is easy to miss: it is not "included in your plan." It's a consumption product layered on top of seats you're already paying for.

Monthly credits are $10 per 1,000, shared across your workspace, and they reset monthly without rollover. If you buy on an annual term instead, annual credits cost $13 per 1,000 — 30% more per credit, which is the opposite of the usual annual discount. And a Free or Plus workspace can't simply buy credits to add Custom Agents.

The credit math varies with what the agent does. Each run uses credits, and the amount depends on how much the agent reads, how many steps it takes, how often it runs and which model it uses. Credits are shared, so every Custom Agent draws from the same balance no matter who created or ran it.

Notion publishes worked examples per agent type. A Q&A agent is listed at about $0.03–$0.11 per run; a status update agent at about $0.08–$0.18; a daily brief agent at about $0.10–$0.30. Run that status update agent 60 times a month and you're at $4.80–$10.80 — one agent, one narrow job, with a 2.25x spread between the low and high end of Notion's own estimate.

### When you run out, the agents just stop

This is a detail worth checking before you buy. If your workspace doesn't have enough credits, Custom Agents pause automatically until credits reset or an admin adds more — and premium models pause too. Admins get in-app and email notifications at 80% and 100% of credit usage, so there's time to adjust before agents pause.

So the system has a documented failure mode. Notion's mitigation is an alert, which means someone has to be watching.

### There are two separate meters, and one of them isn't the one you think

Notion runs a general AI usage allowance *and* a credit system, and they don't overlap. Business and Enterprise include a usage allowance for certain AI features, measured in a six-hour window and a monthly window, covering the personal Notion Agent, image generation and page translation; if the allowance is used up, those features pause until the window refreshes. It does not cover AI Meeting Notes, which has its own 10-hour daily cap, or Custom Agents, Workers and premium models, which spend credits.

One thing Notion does not do: publish the size of that allowance. The numbers for either window aren't public, so you find your ceiling by hitting it. Admins can soften that — there's a setting to allow the workspace to use Notion credits after the AI limit is reached, letting members continue by spending credits.

Workers — the code layer — are cheaper per unit. Notion puts Workers at about $0.0023 per run, roughly 4,348 runs per 1,000 monthly credits, cheaper than Custom Agents because they don't require AI decision-making. Workers use micro credits because they run predictable, repeatable code; Custom Agents usually use more because they rely on AI to think through decisions and next steps. Worth noting that rate isn't live yet: Notion had said Workers would start requiring credits on 15 October 2026, but as of 23 October 2026 its help centre still says no credits are used during the beta, with no new date given.

### Notion has built a whole governance layer for spend

Notion provides admin tooling for cost control. You can set credit limits for individual Custom Agents so they pause at a threshold, though an agent already mid-task is allowed to finish before new usage stops. Admins can also pause or switch off an agent at any time to stop credit usage immediately. A simple agent running hourly can cost more than a complex one running weekly, so frequency, not complexity, is the number to watch.

## The Counterpoint

![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-custom-agents-2026s-most-overhyped-ai-tool/4.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/understand-pricing-for-workers))*

The strongest argument against my read: metered pricing is a straightforward way to pay for what you use instead of a flat seat fee for capacity you don't touch. Notion gives you real levers — per-agent credit limits, the ability to kill an agent mid-month, and cheap Workers for deterministic jobs. A low-volume agent at Notion's published rates costs a few dollars a month.

That's fair, and I'm not calling this a scam. But a product that requires a spend-governance practice carries overhead the marketing doesn't mention.

## Bottom Line

If you're a solo user or a small team, you can't buy credits on Free or Plus anyway. Check whether the included AI for search and drafting, plus deterministic automation (a Worker, a scheduled sync, or plain templates), covers you before upgrading for Custom Agents.

If you're 25+ people with genuinely high-volume repetitive work, do this before you commit: pick one agent, watch it in the credits dashboard, multiply cost-per-run by realistic monthly runs, and set a per-agent limit on day one. If the number isn't obviously less than the labor it replaces, don't scale it.

## FAQ

**Are Notion's Custom Agents included in the Business plan?**
No. They're available on Business and Enterprise, priced under the credit system at $10 per 1,000 monthly credits, on top of your seats. The general AI usage allowance doesn't cover Custom Agents or Workers.

**What happens if my workspace runs out of credits?**

Custom Agents pause automatically until credits reset or an admin adds more, and premium models pause too.

You'll get in-app and email alerts at 80% and 100% usage.

**Are Workers cheaper than agents?**
Yes, at the published rate. Notion puts Workers at about $0.0023 per run — roughly 4,348 runs per 1,000 monthly credits, because they run predictable, repeatable code rather than AI reasoning. As of 23 October 2026 the help centre still describes Workers as not consuming credits during beta.

**Do unused credits carry over?**
No. They're shared across your workspace and reset monthly without rollover.

**Is any of this a reason to leave Notion?**
This covers one feature, not the platform. Notion's core workspace is unaffected; just don't budget for agents as if they were included.

*Updated October 2026. This post is my analysis of Notion's published pricing and help documentation, not a hands-on test. Sources: [Notion pricing](https://www.notion.com/pricing), [Custom Agents pricing help](https://www.notion.com/help/custom-agent-pricing), [Notion credits dashboard](https://www.notion.com/help/track-usage-in-the-notion-credits-dashboard), [Notion AI usage allowance](https://www.notion.com/help/manage-your-usage-allowance-for-notion-ai), [Workers pricing](https://www.notion.com/help/understand-pricing-for-workers).*

## My Take

![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-custom-agents-2026s-most-overhyped-ai-tool/3.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/manage-your-usage-allowance-for-notion-ai))*

My read: the marketing frames Custom Agents as removing work, and adopting them adds one back — someone has to own the credit dashboard. That's not fatal, but it's a real job, and I think teams should name the person before they build the second agent, not after the first invoice.

The part I'd push back on hardest is the pricing structure, not the price. $10 per 1,000 credits is cheap next to an hour of anyone's time. But the cost scales with frequency, and frequency is the thing people tune last and casually. Change a trigger from daily to hourly and you've multiplied the bill by 24 without touching the agent's logic. Set a per-agent limit on day one specifically so that mistake is capped.

Pausing is the other thing I'd plan for. If a weekly client roll-up stops because an unrelated agent drained the shared pool, you find out when the client does. The 80% and 100% alerts help, but they go to admins, not to the person who depends on the output.

The fair concession: Notion publishes enough detail — per-run ranges by agent type, a per-run rate for Workers, a usage dashboard — that you can actually do unit economics before you spend. Most AI vendors don't. The number I'd want is cost per run times realistic monthly runs, compared against the labor it replaces, and if that comparison isn't obvious, the answer is no.

I'm not an accountant or a financial adviser, and none of this is financial advice — the figures here are Notion's published list prices, and your bill depends on what your agents actually do.
